eve_support: Hey team, customer seeing intermittent 500s on text-generation but says they can't find any trace token in their UI. Can someone paste a short repro ask we can share with a non-technical user? :thinking:
sam_eng: Sure — keep it tiny. Ask for (A) a screenshot of the browser network panel where the request is made, (B) an exported HAR or curl, or (C) the debug token from our Console if they can click help -> Send debug bundle. For non-technical people, screenshot + small curl is easiest.
lee_oncall: Quick checklist to send to customer (one message they can copy):

1) If you can open Chrome: Open DevTools (F12) -> Network -> reproduce the error -> right-click the failed request -> "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL" -> paste into the reply.
2) If you can't do that: take a screenshot of the request row in Network (showing status, URL and headers).
3) Optionally: Export a HAR (Network -> right-click -> Save all as HAR) and attach.
4) If you have access to the Redwood Console: go to Console -> Requests, find the failed request time, click it and copy the top-level "Trace ID" value and paste here.

support-bot: NOTE: If a trace ID is attached we can look up the backend span and kv cache metrics immediately.

customer_alex: I'm not very technical — how do I get that "Copy as cURL" thing?
eve_support: No worries, Alex — here's two ultra-minimal options you can try, pick one:

OPTION A — screenshot (easiest):
- Open the page where the error happened.
- Press F12 (or right-click -> Inspect) -> click "Network" tab.
- Reproduce the action that gives the 500.
- Look for the request in the list with status 500. Take a screenshot of the whole DevTools window (so we can see headers/time). Attach here.

OPTION B — copy as curl (one-line you can paste):
- Same steps to find the request in Network. Right-click the request -> Copy -> "Copy as cURL". Paste the text you copied into this thread.

If you can paste the curl, we can run it locally (we'll strip any secrets). If you're not comfortable pasting full auth headers, hide the Authorization value with <redacted> and still paste the rest.

sam_eng: If they can run a quick curl themselves to reproduce (no auth required for public repro), give them this minimal example to run and paste output: 

```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" \\n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Tell them to paste the curl stdout + stderr (or a screenshot) back.

lee_oncall: For mobile apps: if it's iOS ask them to capture a short screen recording while reproducing and attach it. For Android, ask for adb logcat output around the time of the failure — they can run `adb logcat | grep TraceToken` if the SDK prints it. If they don't know adb, a screen recording + approximate local time is fine.

customer_alex: I can only do screenshots. Where in the Console is the "Trace ID"?
eve_support: In the Console -> Requests list, click the row for the error (use the timestamp you saw), then look on the right-hand details pane for "Trace ID" or "Trace token" field. It looks like a short hex/uuid (e.g. 7f3a2b1c). Copy that string and paste here. If you can't find it, attach the screenshot and we'll pull it from the HAR or curl.

sam_eng: Internal tip for us: if we get the Trace ID we should check: (1) request span in tracing UI, (2) upstream model host response and latency, (3) whether the request hit a fallback/quantized model.

lee_oncall: Also ask customer to include approximate local time (HH:MM and timezone) of the failed attempt and which region they were using. That speeds lookup when they can't supply trace id.

customer_alex: Ok attaching screenshot now. Thanks!
eve_support: Awesome — thanks Alex. Once you attach the screenshot I'll look up any trace we can correlate and follow up with exact span ids and a minimal curl we can use to reproduce internally. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Reminder to triage: label thread with "needs-trace" and add to escalation queue if no trace present after 12h.
